title: Rational and Radical Equations
seo_title: Rational and Radical Equations Worksheet: Extraneous Solutions (Algebra 2, A-REI.A.2) | 100 Questions
standard_text: Solve simple rational and radical equations in one variable, and give examples showing how extraneous solutions may arise.
meta_desc: Free Algebra 2 worksheet on rational and radical equations: proportions, extraneous solutions, square and cube root equations, rational exponents and work problems. 100 questions.
key_big: Clear fractions with the LCD; isolate a radical and raise both sides to its power.
key_sub: Always check: answers that make a denominator 0 or a root negative are extraneous.
body_html:
How it works

To solve a rational equation, multiply every term by the LCD to clear the fractions, solve, and then check: a solution that makes any denominator 0 is extraneous and must be thrown out.

To solve a radical equation, isolate the radical, then raise both sides to the same power (square for √, cube for ∛). Squaring can create extraneous solutions, so check every answer in the original equation.

For work problems, add the rates (jobs per hour): 1/a + 1/b = 1/t.

Example

Solve √(x + 7) = x + 1.

Square: x + 7 = x² + 2x + 1

x² + x − 6 = 0, so x = 2 or −3

Check −3: √4 = 2 but −3 + 1 = −2. Extraneous.

Answer: x = 2

Example

One worker takes 4 hours, another takes 6 hours. How long together?

1/4 + 1/6 = 5/12 per hour

Answer: 12/5 = 2.4 hours

Common mistakes

  • Keeping a solution that makes a denominator 0.
  • Squaring term by term: (x + 1)² is x² + 2x + 1, not x² + 1.
  • Squaring before isolating the radical.
  • Adding or averaging the times in a work problem instead of adding the rates.

faq.a: A value that comes out of the algebra but does not satisfy the original equation, usually because it makes a denominator zero or a square root negative.

faq.q: How do you solve a rational equation?
faq.a: Multiply both sides by the least common denominator, solve the resulting equation, and check each answer in the original.

faq.q: How do you solve a radical equation?
faq.a: Isolate the radical, raise both sides to the index (square a square root), solve, and check for extraneous solutions.

faq.q: How do you solve a work problem?
faq.a: Add the rates. If one person takes a hours and another takes b hours, together they do 1/a + 1/b of the job each hour.

items.q: Solve 3x − 1 = 6x − 5.
items.e: Cross-multiply: 3(x − 5) = 6(x − 1). Then 3x − 15 = 6x − 6, so x = −3. Check: it does not make a denominator 0.

items.q: Solve 7x + 6 = 28x + 3.
items.e: Cross-multiply: 7(x + 3) = 28(x + 6). Then 7x + 21 = 28x + 168, so x = −7. Check: it does not make a denominator 0.

items.q: Solve 2x + 1 = 8x − 2.
items.e: Cross-multiply: 2(x − 2) = 8(x + 1). Then 2x − 4 = 8x + 8, so x = −2. Check: it does not make a denominator 0.

items.q: Solve 4x + 2 = 8x − 3.

items.q: Solve x²x − 4 = −2x + 24x − 4.
items.e: Multiply both sides by (x − 4): x² = −2x + 24, so (x + 6)(x − 4) = 0 and x = 4 or −6. But x = 4 makes the denominator 0, so it is extraneous. x = −6.

items.q: Solve x − 12x = 4.
items.e: Multiply by x: x² − 4x − 12 = 0, so (x + 2)(x − 6) = 0. Neither solution is 0, so both work. x = −2, 6.

items.q: Solve x²x + 5 = −7x − 10x + 5.
items.e: Multiply both sides by (x + 5): x² = −7x − 10, so (x + 2)(x + 5) = 0 and x = −5 or −2. But x = −5 makes the denominator 0, so it is extraneous. x = −2.

items.q: Solve 16 + 1x = 12.
items.e: 1x = 12 − 16 = 13, so x = 3. (Subtracting denominators, 6 − 2, is a common mistake.)

Cube both sides: 2x − 5 = −27, so x = −11. A cube root can equal a negative number.
